parole.significato: A member of an indigenous people related to the Sioux living in the Great Plains in the United States and Canada.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from French Assiniboine, a transcription of Ojibwe asinii-bwaan (“stone Sioux”)/ᐊᓯᓃᑇᐣ.

parole.significato: Any North American freshwater fish of certain species of the genus Coregonus that live in cold-water lakes.
parole.testo: From French ciscoette (“siscowet”), from Ojibwe siscowet (“cooks itself”).

parole.significato: The rattlesnake Sistrurus catenatus (formerly Crotalinus catenatus) in the family Viperidae, found in three subspecies.
parole.testo: Possibly from the Mississagi River (Ontario, Canada), from French Mississague, Missisague (also Oumisagai, Michisaguek), from Ojibwe misiza:gi: (“inhabitant of the great river mouth, that is, the Mississagi River”). Doublet of Mississauga.

parole.significato: A member of an Algonquian people now living in southern Ontario, Canada; also a member of this race.
parole.testo: From French Mississague, from Ojibwe misizaagii (“inhabitant of large river mouth”) (with reference to the area where the Mississauga River drains into Lake Huron). Doublet of massasauga.

parole.significato: A large freshwater gamefish of the pike family, native to the lakes and rivers of eastern and middle western North Amer…
parole.testo: From French masque allongé (literally “long mask”), a corruption of Ojibwe maashkinoozhe (literally “ugly pike”) or Algonquin maskinunga. Not related to German Muskel (“muscle”) or Lunge (“lung”).
